simple.meaning: מָצַץ (mâtsats) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to suck.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Isaiah, beginning at Isaiah 66:11. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מָצַץ (H4711) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: מָצַץ (mâtsats) / H4711 is traced through Isaiah 66:11 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H4711. matsats [ מָצַץ ] verb drain out (compare מָצָה ; Late Hebrew id. ; Arabic suck, suck up ; Aramaic , מְצַץ suck or press out) ; — only Qal Imperfect 2masculine plural תָּמֹ֫צּוּ כְּבוֺדָהּ מִוִּיז וְהִתְעַנַּגְתֶּם Isa 66:11 that ye may drain out and delight yourselves , etc. (|| וּשְׂבַעְתֶּם תִּינְקוּ ).
